values: Materials and setup｜A1—A5 are entirely fictional and do not correspond to real jurisdictions or product rules
Use 30 minutes to complete the D1 pre-filing paper review: read the product and materials, list evidence differences, and write the pause and escalation; do not make a real filing based on it.
A1｜The fictional product D1 plans to enter the M1 market, and material directory version 3 lists six required documents; this is only an exercise assumption and does not represent any real category.

A2｜Of the six documents in the directory, four are marked verified and two are pending: the test report T1 has no final signature yet, and the applicable product version of the clinical or use evidence E1 is unverified.
A3｜The label L2 states the function claim C1, and the technical material V3 covers only C0; without original evidence or approval supporting C1, the label is not written as compliant.

A4｜The regulatory index lists both the effective text R1 and the proposed text R2, and R2 is not yet in force; the applicable date and jurisdiction must be verified, and proposed requirements must not be written as current law.

A5｜The submission draft is marked “ready to send”, but the quality sign-off Q1 and the regulatory sign-off RA1 are both blank; all differences remain open, and authorized personnel decide whether to add evidence, revise, or postpone.
Tasks and deliverables
Verify six documents with four verified and two pending; list T1/E1, the L2 claim C1, R1/R2, and the Q1/RA1 sign-off status separately.
Submit a one-page evidence matrix, version differences, and pending approval list; do not write that marketing authorization or a formal regulatory response has been obtained.
Reference answer (complete it independently first)
Of the six required documents, four are verified and two are pending; numerical completeness is not evidence validity.
T1 lacks the final signature and the E1 version is unclear; the L2 claim C1 is not directly supported by the C0 scope of V3.
R2 is proposed text and cannot serve as an effective requirement; Q1 and RA1 are blank, so the submission status should be pending and handed to authorized personnel.
Boundaries and review

D1, M1, R1/R2, and all materials are fictional. Real classification, regulatory applicability, trials, quality release, external submission, or recall are judged by professionals per product and jurisdiction authorization.

description.text: How do regulatory affairs managers develop filing strategy, verify regulatory evidence, and hand off audits and recalls? Plus the definitions behind US broad occupation wages and projections, the Chinese wage gap, and a fictional filing material exercise.

subject.name: Regulatory affairs managers
subject.summary: Develops product regulatory strategy and filing plans, coordinates review of materials submitted to regulatory agencies, responds to regulatory questions, and coordinates development, quality, production, and marketing teams. The specific product, market, and applicable rules determine the submission requirements; a manager title does not automatically confer legal opinion, product release, or regulatory sign-off authority.
